issue_context.title: BUG: Never end up with numpy string dtypes
issue_context.body:
- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the latest version of pandas.

- [x] (optional) I have confirmed this bug exists on the master branch of pandas.

---

**Note**: Please read [this guide](https://matthewrocklin.com/blog/work/2018/02/28/minimal-bug-reports) detailing how to provide the necessary information for us to reproduce your bug.

#### Code Sample, a copy-pastable example

```python
DataFrame(["foo", "bar", "baz"]).astype(bytes)

```
As discussed in #39484 we do not want to get numpy string dtypes here. This should have dtype object
comments: this is a breaking change, but was never intended and we have 0 support for S (or B) types as native pandas types.

Can we deprecate this in some way first?

And what do you exactly want to change? Only the resulting dtype to be object (but still do the conversion to bytes), or actually disallow casting to bytest altogether?
One option would be to deprecate `astype(bytes)` or `astype(np.dtype("S"))`, and let users use another method to actually convert values to bytes (eg `s.map(bytes)` might also do that?)
Related: when we pass a np.dtype("S") ndarray to Series or DataFrame do we cast to object?  ATM we do this for only a few variants of the DataFrame constructor, not for Series

review_comments: can the commented-out code be removed?
i think we ought to have a sanitize_str_dtypes or something akin to sanitize_to_nanoseconds
There is a `_sanitize_str_dtypes`, but not fully sure it does exactly what we want here
This is now done as part of maybe_coerce_values, though that may be more heavy-weight than we want here

I think this commented out code was from the initial implementation at which point I only supported storing EAs in the ArrayManager, and not numpy.ndarrays. But now both are supported, so you can remove this code.
